_comment: SPARK — S165 P4: atlas specs for the six TIER-3 TOWERS, four CONDITIONS each.
⭐ THE CASTLE PATTERN, DELIBERATELY. A tower is a STRUCTURE with conditions, not a character with
actions: framesPerState 1, fit 'box', and every state a `still` PNG rather than a clip. Copied from
assets-source/race-castles/atlas-specs.json, whose own note gives the reason — a building has no
gait, no swing and no idle bob, so a clip would spend veo's whole budget re-drawing a static
subject and buy back two failure modes this pipeline has already paid for twice (seed drift over
the length of a clip, and outright generation failure).
⭐ fit 'box', NOT 'height'. Height-fit exists to keep CHARACTERS comparable by how tall they look.
These six are different shapes on purpose — a squat wide crag, a low basin, a tall obelisk — and
box-fit keeps each one whole inside its cell instead of scaling a wide building down by its width.
⚠ normaliseStateScale is NOT set here and must not be. It equalises the SEED-FRAME size across
states, which is right when four clips of one character disagree about zoom. These four states are
four separate DRAWINGS of a building in different conditions, and a destroyed tower is SUPPOSED to
be smaller than an intact one — normalising would inflate the rubble back to full height.
⚠ THE DESTRUCTION CINEMATICS ARE A SEPARATE ATLAS (destroy-specs.json), because they are animated
and these are not: framesPerState is a per-spec value, so one file cannot hold both.
_white_limit: ⛔ enclosedWhiteLimitPct 4e-05 — S165, after the owner spotted white patches: "some of them have
that white background because not cut out too well" and "look at the tower cut out and destroction
video some of them still have some white backgrounds small parts too". He was right on both.
THE CAUSE WAS AN OMISSION, NOT A TUNING ERROR: these specs never set the knob at all, so they took
build-sprite-atlas.mjs's DEFAULT of 0.003 — which is 75x more permissive than the 4e-05 the race
units were tuned to in S164. Enclosed near-white BELOW the limit is deliberately KEPT (that is what
saves eyes and blade glints), so a loose limit ships background pockets as opaque white blobs.
⭐ MEASURED, AND THE METRIC THAT MATTERS IS LARGEST POCKET, NOT TOTAL. At 4e-05 the units carry
66-768 px of near-white in TOTAL but their biggest single pocket is 2-52 px — eye glints, correctly
kept. The castles and towers at 0.003 had biggest pockets of 113-168 px, which is a visible patch.
⭐ AND AN AGGRESSIVE LIMIT IS SAFER ON A STRUCTURE THAN ON A CHARACTER. A character has eyes and
teeth to protect, which is the whole reason the knob exists and why the orc needed its own value.
sharedStyle here already forbids anything white or near-white ON the building, so by construction
every near-white pocket in one of these frames is background.
